_comment: BOTH SETTINGS WERE FORCED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT PREFERENCE.
seq 4096 was tried and OOMs at step 3:
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: out of memory
in unsloth_zoo/gradient_checkpointing.py, resizing the offload buffer.
It survives two steps and dies when a batch of longer samples arrives.
The earlier budget that said 4096 had 2.66 GB spare counted the 4-bit weights,
the adapter and the lm_head logits tensor - and missed the gradient-checkpoint
offload buffers, which also scale with sequence length. Those consumed the
margin. Arithmetic is not a substitute for a smoke test.
It was also slow at 4096: 240-268 s/step, about 180 hours for 2 epochs, because
'smartly offload gradients' was shuttling gradients to CPU RAM every step.
keep_reasoning FALSE roughly halves tokens per sample. That cuts the work per
step AND the activation memory, so it buys speed and headroom together.
lm_head stays in target_modules and is not negotiable: token 151657
(<tool_call>) sits at the 0.2 percentile by norm in every Qwen base checked,
and without training it the model emits 0% parseable tool calls. Measured.
SMOKE-TEST FIVE STEPS before committing. Two is not enough - 4096 passed two.
